1 1. Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that on 16.03.2021, at about 11:30 a.m., petitioner Deepak along with his sister Asha had gone to Patparganj in search of a job.

It has been alleged that when they were going towards Azad apartment, in front of gate no. 2 of the Max hospital, Patparganj,
Delhi, near metro pillar no. 211, within the jurisdiction of PS Madhu Vihar, a motorcycle (make Bullet) came from Shani Mandir side at a very fast speed and hit the petitioner and his sister, due to which the latter fell down on the road and came under the wheels of one incoming truck bearing registration no. DL-1GC-2946 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle).

It has been further alleged that the said offending vehicle (truck) was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, in a rash and negligent manner without taking necessary precautions at the time of the accident.
The injured Deepak was thereon immediately taken to Max Healthcare, Delhi for initial treatment, where his MLC was prepared vide MLC No. 11444.
An FIR in this regard was also registered vide FIR no. 58/21, for the offences u/s 279/337/304-A IPC, at PS Madhu Vihar, Delhi.
The present DAR petition thereon came to be filed in due course for the petitioner and against the respondents on 18.05.2022.
WS / Reply of Respondents 2.

The respondent no. 1 i.e. the driver of the offending vehicle, failed to file his WS despite being granted several opportunities, due to which his right to file WS/reply to the DAR stood closed by the Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 28.09.2022.
3. Respondent no. 2 i.e. EDMC, being the owner of the offending vehicle, filed its WS wherein it has been contended that the petitioners have filed a HARUN PRATAP Date:
PRATAP 2026.01.03 16:57:12 +0530 false and frivolous case against the respondent and that the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation

. It has been further contended that no accident took place by the vehicle of the answering respondent no.
2 as the victim got hit by one motorcycle, while his sister was subsequently got hit by the MCD vehicle.
It has been further contended that the respondent no. 2 has been falsely implicated in the present case and thus the R-2 prayed for dismissal of the DAR petition.
ISSUES 4.

From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 28.09.2022, as under:-
(i) Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 16.03.2021 at about 11:30 am near Max hospital, PPG Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Madhu Vihar due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. DL1GC-2946 being driven by respondent no. 1/driver ?
OPP (ii) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP.

Since there were two victims who either died or suffered injury in the accident in question, hence,
two separate DAR qua each of them came to be filed before the Tribunal.

Both the two DARs were subsequently directed to be consolidated and common evidence was directed to be recorded and kept in main case file bearing MACT No. 184/22, by Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 22.02.2023.

Petitioners did not examine any other witness and PE stood closed by the Tribunal vide order dated 17.01.2025, in view of the separate statement of Ld. Counsel for petitioners recorded to this effect.
RESPONDENT'S EVIDENCE 9.

No evidence was led by the respondent no. 1 and 2 to prove their defence in this case and RE stood closed vide order dated 06.03.2025, in view of the separate statement of Ld. Counsel for R1 recorded to this effect.
10. Final arguments heard.
File perused.
Issue wise findings Issue no.1

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 16.03.2021 at about 11:30 am near Max hospital, PPG Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Madhu Vihar due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. DL1GC-2946 being driven by respondent no. 1/driver ? OPP 11.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2026.01.03 16:57:25 +0530 can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1)
SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
12.

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioner has examined himself as the star witness to prove the contentions regarding the claim for compensation as PW-1.

The said witness has categorically stated in his examination on oath that he was hit by a motorcycle rider and there is not a whisper regarding the petitioner being hit by the offending vehicle i.e. MCD truck.

Though, it has been observed in the connected matter after perusal of the CCTV footage of the incident that the driver of the offending vehicle was rash and negligent in his driving at the time of the accident, but the offending vehicle is neither seen nor stated to have hit the petitioner herein.
Furthermore, it is pertinent to note that the petitioner has not impleaded the bullet motorcycle rider who is stated to have hit the petitioner and thus caused injuries to him.

In absence of any averment to this fact that the simple injuries to the Dar - Deepak vs Shyam Singh on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10270954/
4 petitioner were caused after being hit by the offending vehicle driven by R1 at the time of the accident, the Tribunal has no hesitation in hereby arriving at the finding that the petitioner has failed to prove his claim for compensation against the respondents.
Therefore, the issue at hand is decided in favour of the respondents and against the petitioner accordingly.

The onus to prove this issue was on the petitioner.
However, in view of the findings on issue no. 1 as aforesaid, the Tribunal has no hesitation in hereby arriving at the finding that the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.
Therefore, the issue at hand is hereby decided against the petitioner and in favour of the respondents accordingly.
ISSUE NO.3/ RELIEF 14.
In view of the the findings on the aforesaid issues, the claim petition filed on behalf of the petitioner is hereby dismissed being devoid of any merits.

Copy of this order be also sent to concerned court of Ld. JMFC and DLSA.
